summary: U.S. equities traded mixed on Tuesday, August 25, as investors weighed fresh trade tensions and awaited key catalysts. President Trump announced 50% tariffs on Canadian automotive imports effective January 1, 2027, prompting Canada to announce retaliatory measures. Markets brushed aside the trade headwinds initially, with tech stocks rebounding as the 10-year yield dipped. Dick's Sporting Goods plummeted 17% after slashing full-year guidance, while financials rallied on improving capital markets activity. Crypto markets extended their rally, with Bitcoin briefly touching $81,000—its highest level since May—driven by Treasury bond buyback announcements and expectations around the Clarity Act vote in September. Investors are now eyeing Wednesday's Nvidia earnings and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole speech for directional clues, as well as the upcoming PCE inflation data.

signals.title: Trump slaps Canada with 50% automotive tariffs
signals.desc: President Trump announced 50% tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, parts, and steel effective January 2027, escalating trade tensions and raising input cost concerns for U.S. manufacturers.

signals.title: Bitcoin breaks $81,000 on Treasury buyback tailwinds
signals.desc: Bitcoin hit a three-month high as the Treasury doubled its long-term bond buyback program and Trump pushed for crypto legislation, injecting liquidity and suppressing yields.

signals.title: Dick's Sporting Goods crashes on guidance cut
signals.desc: DKS tumbled 17% after missing Q2 earnings and slashing its full-year profit outlook, signaling consumer discretionary weakness in the sporting goods sector.

signals.title: Markets await Nvidia earnings and Warsh's Jackson Hole speech
signals.desc: Investors are positioning ahead of Wednesday's Nvidia Q2 report and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's debut Jackson Hole remarks, both of which could determine near-term market direction.

signals.title: Financials rally on capital markets strength
signals.desc: Jefferies Financial gained 5.5% amid a broader financial sector rally driven by improving investment banking activity and rising market volatility.

verdict: Markets are in a holding pattern ahead of Nvidia earnings and Warsh's Jackson Hole debut, with crypto strength and trade tensions creating cross-currents.
